correctness.rationale: The stationary two-sided iid binary coding and a bounded endpoint identity reduce the paired quantile sum to reversal-odd finite-block sums. All length-one to length-three reversal-odd words have explicit de Bruijn graph potentials. On four-bit words, the displayed potential works exactly when L(h)=0; subtracting L(h) times the 0010/0100 signed indicator proves the full rank-one decomposition. Exact rational counting yields covariance (1/8,-1/32,-1/64,0) and variance 1/32. Finite dependence and a standard CLT prove the Gaussian limit; zero-L sums telescope. The Rosenblatt conjugacy and independent full-branch tent codings give the same-target contrast. Actual standalone verify.py passed a complete finite symbol calculus, separately from the analytical infinite-time argument.

value.rationale: The result resolves a natural statistical-identifiability and sampling-efficiency issue left by prescribed-density conjugacy: even for identical stationary laws, some paired quantile errors cancel exactly in time while the alternative product-tent sampler has iid errors. The rank-one six-dimensional diffusion quotient is a structural classification, not a mere small example. It proves the first nonvanishing binary resolution and all fifteen level-four thresholds, and supplies a precise universal CLT coefficient. The finite cutoff is motivated by the first failure of the cohomological cancellation, not by arbitrary parameter slicing.
